instruction.text: Create a compound sentence by adding a conjunction.

hint.text:
Compound sentences are sentences that combine two or more sentences.

Conjunctions are joining words. They join groups of words or sentences together.

atoms.a: Leave the flat at 8am sharp. Bring the cat to the vet.

feedback.wrong: A comma is added between two independent clauses when they are connected with a coordinating conjunction.

atoms.a: Skateboarding is super fun! don’t forget to wear a helmet!
Our art teacher is kind and understanding. We always feel at ease in her class.
I’m not going to yoga class today. I normally go twice a week.

instruction.text: Drag the conjunctions to the correct category. Select a conjunction to hear an example sentence.

hint.text:
Subordinating conjunctions connect unequal clauses. This means that one clause is dependent, while the other is independent.
For example: Leilani and Khalil exchanged ideas for the book while eating at the café.

Coordinating conjunctions connect two equal clauses.
For example: It rained all day, yet everyone came to the football game.
hint.sound: Subordinating conjunctions connect unequal clauses. This means that one clause is dependent, while the other is independent. atoms.sound: I watched TV while doing my homework.
After I had finished football, I played in the park.
Even though I’m tired, I’m still going to meet my friends.
I have played the clarinet since I was 5.
I love my best friend, for he is kind and caring.
I like dancing and I love singing.
I hadn’t washed the dishes, nor had I tidied my room.
I like reading but I really hate writing.
I couldn’t sleep so I red my book.
The weather was terrible, yet we still had a barbecue.

instruction.text: Select the correct subordinating conjunction to complete the sentence.

atoms.b: ((--Because Although --Since)) it is raining, I still have to walk my dog.
My grandpa dances ((whenever --unless --until)) there is a family celebration.
I couldn’t do my homework ((until --as_soon_as --though)) Fluffy got off of my notebooks.
((When --Although --Unless)) our coach calls a time-out, we gather around him and pay close attention.

instruction.text: Which type of conjunction is used in the following sentence?

atoms.a: The food was still hot, even though Amelia had blown on it for 2 minutes!
I’m on my way to school, but I forgot my pencil case.
Since you’re a huge basketball fan, you should try to get tickets for next week’s match.
